A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedGMR research, despite the changed title and organization. All 37 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables, and rendered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-learning simulations on FEMNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-100, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, aggregation experiments, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the three image datasets and StackOverflow, together with component ablations, transfer experiments, patience sweeps, and fixed-time restoration comparisons.

M1.justification: The described procedure loses an explicit stage: v1 Section 4.1 and Algorithm 2 adapt initial densities using a timing-error optimization, whereas v2 Algorithm 1 accepts initial densities and performs restoration without that optimization. Appendix H.3 also introduces a fixed-time restoration variant. Plateau-triggered restoration, importance-based pruning, mask-aware aggregation, and IMS otherwise remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds StackOverflow next-token language modeling with a Transformer under IID and user-wise non-IID settings. This extends evaluation from image classification to text prediction; FEMNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-100 remain.

E2.justification: The six main baselines and the MA/GA/FA aggregation comparison are retained. New supplementary comparisons include Aux and Aux+GMR variants of HeteroFL, FjORD, FedRolex, and FIARSE in Figure 4, plus fixed-time restoration in Table 10. Removing v1's post-training pruning experiment also removes its FedAsync comparison.

E3.justification: The reported CIFAR-10 evaluation budget changes from 180k to 220k seconds, while total training budgets change from 310k to 250k for CIFAR-10 and 320k to 280k for ImageNet-100. The evaluation cutoff is described as stabilization of most methods instead of FedGMR alone. New protocols include token-level language-model evaluation, patience sweeps, and fixed-progress restoration. These reported changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds restoration-transfer experiments across four MHFL families, quantitative patience sweeps, and fixed-time versus early-stopping restoration controls in Appendix H. It removes v1's post-training pruning/compactness study and replaces the detailed client-wise training-dynamics presentation. Component ablations, aggregation comparisons, and the IMS scaling experiment remain, with the component table moved to Appendix G.

E5.justification: The stated mean and standard deviation change from 11 nearby test evaluations in a symmetric ±5 window to 20 evaluations in a ±10 window. This changes temporal uncertainty estimation; neither version establishes independent repeated-run counts or random seeds.

E6.justification: Many baseline, component-ablation, and aggregation results are replaced, and StackOverflow and restoration-control results are added. For example, Table 1's High non-IID ImageNet-100 entries change from 59.72% to 58.01% for FedGMR and 29.78% to 15.26% for FedRolex. These are revised reported results under changed smoothing, not established same-protocol performance losses. The IMS timing values remain unchanged, while the post-training pruning results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix E.5's asynchronous decomposition, proposition, proof, and participation-skew/staleness perturbation analysis, explicitly qualified as preliminary. It also revises synchronous derivations, including changing the non-IID bias denominator from squared minimum coverage in v1 Equation 79 to first-power coverage in v2 Equation 59. The initial-density timing-gradient derivation is removed. The post-plateau lemma is retained through relocation from Appendix C to A.

C1.justification: v2's introduction explicitly broadens the contribution to restoration that transfers across different MHFL pruning and sub-model construction strategies, and its abstract and conclusion extend empirical claims to text tasks. The central capacity-bottleneck, gradual-restoration, and density-dependent convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 calls asynchrony essential; v2 explains task-dependent benefits, possible synchronous advantages, and participation-skew/staleness costs. It adds interpretations about trigger independence and portability, while dropping the compactness interpretation. Auxiliary-module discussion becomes more qualified, but Appendix G misattributes 56.50% to removing buffering: Table 7 reports 60.62% without buffering and 56.50% without both buffering and IMS.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a detailed StackOverflow recipe, including user/sample counts, vocabulary, sequence length, Transformer configuration, training settings, and token-accuracy calculation. It adds an explicit code repository URL in place of v1's anonymous supplementary-code/notebook disclosure. Conversely, v1's per-setting optimal-patience table and fixed ablation-patience row are removed, reducing specificity for reproducing retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on slimmable networks, fixed sparse masks, and hypothesis classes, trims several asynchronous-protocol citations, and newly acknowledges Vahidian et al.'s similar aggregation rule. These refine attribution and motivation while retaining the central positioning around the efficiency–capacity limitation of static MHFL.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative, and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting. The feasibility study moves into the method section, aggregation moves into the workflow, component ablations move to an appendix, and the proof receives a new roadmap and organization. This substantially changes the narrative beyond scientific additions alone.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Benchmark and aggregation tables expand to four tasks; Figure 2 gains a language-model panel; Figure 3 becomes a four-task average-density ablation display. v2 adds Figures 4–6 and a notation table, relocates the component-ablation table, and removes several earlier supplementary displays.

improvement.justification: The language benchmark and transfer, patience, and fixed-time controls provide stronger tests of restoration's applicability and mechanism than v1's evidence. The qualified discussion of asynchrony also improves interpretation. These gains are moderated by lost patience-setting details, the new buffering/table mismatch, and a gap in the rewritten variance proof: v2 Equation 45 introduces a final 1/T factor that does not follow from its displayed Jensen steps. The empirical gains therefore support a limited overall improvement.
